raw_annotations.proposed_function: Enhances high-affinity binding to DSR RNA by slowing the off-rate and stabilizing the RNA-bound conformation through hydrophobic contacts with the core YTH domain and N-clamp.
raw_annotations.evidence: Figure 4. A network of interactions is formed between the USR, N-clamp, and core YTH domain. (A) Co-crystal structure of Mmi1 USR-YTH (residues 315–488 modelled) with DSR RNA. Cartoon representation shows protein in blue and RNA in yellow. The USR is shown in darker blue. (B) The conformation of the USR is stabilized by hydrophobic contacts with the core YTH domain and N-clamp. Residues labelled in turquoise either appear or show large chemical shift changes on RNA binding in NMR experiments (see Fig. 5).
raw_annotations.curator_note: Exact positions for the USR (315-326) are explicitly stated in Figure 4 legend and labels. The construct modeled is 315-488.

raw_annotations.proposed_function: The USR, N-clamp, and C-clamps are dynamic in the absence of RNA and become more ordered on RNA-binding, contacting or reinforcing contacts with RNA to enhance affinity.
raw_annotations.evidence: Figure 8. Model for RNA-binding by Mmi1. (A) Schematic diagram showing the contribution of different regions of Mmi1 to DSR RNA-binding. The core conserved YTH fold acts as a platform for RNA-binding but is unable to bind RNA with high affinity alone. The USR, N-clamp and C-clamps have no secondary structure and are dynamic in the absence of RNA (dashed lines). The USR and N-clamp likely exist in an equilibrium between multiple conformers, at least one of which has high affinity for RNA. On RNA-binding these regions become more ordered and contact or reinforce contacts with RNA.
raw_annotations.curator_note: Qualitative mention of USR, N-clamp, and C-clamps as low-complexity/dynamic regions. Specific residue coordinates for N-clamp and C-clamps are not provided in this text snippet, though USR is defined elsewhere in the document.
